messages.author: 181e1e7e113c0a57
messages.subject: correlation residuals
parts:
Hello,
 
 I am interested in obtaining correlation residuals (i.e., standardized covariance resiudals) for a CFA model using DWLS estimation for ordinal data, in order to get an idea of any posisble mispecification. Is it correct to use the resid(fit) command? I am assuming that as the input matrix is of correlations (polychoric) the residuals produced by resid(fit) will automatically be in correlational form. Is that right? Many thanks. Peter

As long as all your observed variables are categorical/ordered: yes.

messages.subject: Re: correlation residuals
parts:
Hi, I've just run the same CFA model in both lavaan and Mplus (a 3 factor cfa with categorical indicators). The results are identical for the most part (same fit statistics, loadings, correlations, etc.). However, the correlation residuals I generate in lavaan through the resid(fit) command differ to those I obtain in mplus with the "output: residual" command. Any thoughts on why this might be or which set of residuals to go with? Many thanks.
 
Peter
 

On Thursday, 17 July 2014 09:16:10 UTC+1, Peter Taylor wrote:
Great, thanks for confirming this
